title: Align quarterly release lanes to OKRs and customer-impact signals
creator: Amina Patel
description: Shape a repeatable, metrics-driven process that maps quarterly product OKRs and customer-impact signals to release lane priorities, capacity reservations, and canary windows across runtime, console, and API surfaces. This ticket creates the spec, acceptance criteria, and cross-functional runbook so PMs can declare priority lanes tied to customer-impact tiers and engineering can pre-book capacity and test plans. The focus is preventing last-minute priority shifts that force unplanned capacity spikes during high-risk launches.
tasks: Define customer-impact signal taxonomy (sev tiers, telemetry sources) and map to OKR categories
Instrument a 'release-priority' signal in Console dashboards using recent incidence and revenue-weighted usage metrics
Create release-lane templates (low/medium/high) with explicit capacity reserve %, canary length, rollback criteria
Work with Infra to add a capacity reservation API and standardized request form for Dedicated pools
Coordinate a runbook template for lane-declared launches: comms, on-call rota, monitoring checklist
Pilot the lane mapping on next quarterly release; run post-mortem and update templates
acceptance_criteria: A taxonomy doc exists and is approved by product, SRE, and customer success
Console dashboard surfaces a release-priority signal and is populated with data for the pilot release
Three lane templates (low/medium/high) are documented with capacity %, canary window, and success/failure gates
Capacity reservation API prototype accepted by Infra and used to book Dedicated quota for pilot
Runbook published in Confluence and validated via a tabletop with on-call, SRE, and Eng leads
Pilot launch completed and a short (2-page) post-mortem with recommended changes is produced
risks: Signal accuracy: telemetry may undercount customer impact for low-telemetry customers
Capacity API timeline slips and blocks Dedicated reservations for pilot
Over-broad lane templates may lead to wasted reserved capacity and increased cost
Stakeholder alignment delays (Sales/CS) could push pilot out of cadence
success_metrics: Pilot completed on schedule with no Sev1 incidents attributable to lane decision
Median 95th latency across runtime endpoints does not degrade more than 5% during pilot
Reserved capacity utilization >= 70% for high-priority lane launches
Time-to-declare lane and reserve capacity reduced to < 5 business days
Post-mortem identifies <= 3 process gaps and incorporates them into runbook
rollout_steps: Week 1: finalize taxonomy and lane templates; review with SRE and Infra
Week 2: instrument dashboard and wire capacity reservation form; engineering kickoff
Week 3-4: Infra implements capacity API prototype; Console exposes signal and alerts
Week 5: tabletop exercise and runbook dry-run with on-call and PMs
Week 6-8: pilot release uses lane process; collect telemetry and cost data
Post-pilot: 1-week retro, update templates, publish stable runbook
notes: Coordinate with PM-314159 to ensure lane naming and tagging are consistent with org-wide launch taxonomy
Prioritize customer accounts with enterprise SLAs for high-priority lane mapping
We will measure cost impact of reservations and iterate on % reserved for each lane
If capacity API is delayed, fallback to manual reservation spreadsheet and documented escalation path
